title: In re the Personal Restraint Petition of
questions: Is the petitioner entitled to have his assault conviction vacated based on double jeopardy principles?

title: Storti v. Univ. of Wash.
questions: Did the University of Washington breach a contractual obligation to its faculty by cancelling, in March of 2009, the 2% "merit pay" raises scheduled to take effect in the 2009-10 academic year?

title: State v. Johnson
questions: This case presents two issues: (1) whether the information charging the crime of unlawful imprisonment must include elements found in the definition of "restrain," and, if so, whether the information in this case fairly included those elements; and (2) whether defense counsel provided effective assistance by proposing that the jury instructions include a generic definition of "reckless" for the crime of assault in the second degree

title: State v. Owens
questions: Does RCW 9A.82.050(1) describe alternative means of committing first degree trafficking in stolen property, and if so, is there substantial evidence to support each of the alternative means?

title: Riverview Cmty. Grp. v. Spencer & Livingston
questions: Should the court dismiss a claim seeking to force the defendants to operate a golf course at a financial loss because the relief sought is too harsh?

title: Schmidt v. Coogan
questions: This case presents multiple issues relating to legal malpractice claims, including the collectibility of an underlying judgment and available damages

title: Campbell v. Dep't of Emp't Sec.
questions: Did the agency err in denying Campbell unemployment benefits under RCW 50.20.050(2)(b)(iii), the "quit to follow" provision

title: LaCoursiere v. Camwest Dev., Inc.
questions: The court must decide whether bonuses, once paid, are wages and if so, whether an employer's profit sharing plan violated the Wage Rebate Act

title: State v. Lindsay
questions: Defendants Lindsay and Holmes were convicted of first degree burglary and robbery, among other things, at a joint trial. The court must decide whether some of the prosecutor's remarks during trial amounted to misconduct that influenced the jury.

title: BAC Home Loans Servicing, LP v. Fulbright
questions: The court considers whether a party is a valid redemptioner when the party recorded its lien before a condominium association brought a judicial foreclosure action

title: State v. Blazina
questions: Did the Court of Appeals err when it declined to consider a challenge to the trial court's imposition of legal financial obligations (LFOs) where the challenge was raised for the first time on appeal?

title: Outsource Servs. Mgmt. v. Nooksack Bus. Corp.
questions: Does a state court have jurisdiction over a contract claim involving an Indian tribe when that tribe waived its sovereign immunity?

title: State v. Crumpton
questions: For a motion for postconviction DNA testing, should the court have to presume the DNA results would be favorable to the convicted individual when deciding whether performing the test might demonstrate that person's innocence?

title: Walston v. Boeing Co.
questions: Is Walston's personal injury action against Boeing for damages stemming from workplace asbestos exposure exempt from the Industrial Insurance Act's exclusive remedy provision on the basis that Boeing deliberately intended the injury?

title: In re Estate of Hambleton
questions: Whether the 2013 amendments to the Estate and Transfer Act may be applied retroactively.

title: State v. Condon
questions: Condon was charged, in the alternative, with first degree murder and felony murder. Was there sufficient evidence to convict him of first degree murder and was he entitled to a lesser included offense jury instruction on second degree murder?

title: Pub. Util. Dist. No. 1 of Okanogan County v. State
questions: The court considers whether public utility districts are authorized to condemn school lands and, if so, whether the particular school lands at issue in this case are exempt from condemnation either because they are held in trust or because they are dedicated to a particular use insofar as they are presently used for cattle grazing. The court also considers the propriety of Conservation Northwest's intervention in the case

title: State v. Medina
questions: Does participation in a King County Community Center Alternative Program constitute "partial confinement," for which an offender is entitled to credit for time served prior to sentencing?

title: Frias v. Asset Foreclosure Servs., Inc.
questions: The Deeds of Trust Act governs nonjudicial foreclosures. Can a person sue for violations of the Deeds of Trust Act before any foreclosure sale has been completed?

title: State v. Lamar
questions: The defendant argues that the trial court's error, failure to instruct the jury to begin deliberations anew after an alternate juror replaced a juror who was ill, is manifest constitutional error that may be raised for the first time on appeal.

title: State v. E.J.J.
questions: Did the defendant's conviction for obstruction of a police officer violate his free speech rights?

title: State v. Russell
questions: Under what circumstances may a police officer frisk a suspect for weapons, and whether that police officer may search a small container found during the frisk?

title: Durland v. San Juan County
questions: Whether neighboring landowners can challenge the issuance of a building permit under 42 U.S.C. §1983 or the Land Use Petition Act? Whether attorney's fees are available under RCW 4.84.370 when a party prevails on jurisdictional grounds?

title: Expedia, Inc. v. Steadfast Ins. Co.
questions: Did the trial court err in delaying ruling on Zurich's duty to defend Expedia from third-party lawsuits pending further discovery of facts relevant to the issue of coverage?

title: State v. Barton
questions: Was the trial court's order requiring the defendant to post 10 percent of his bail amount in cash or other security constitutionally permissible?

title: State v. France
questions: France was convicted of felony harassment. The jury was instructed "threat also means" conduct not proven. Under the law of the case doctrine, should the court reverse his convictions?

title: In re Marriage of Chandola
questions: This case concerns the parenting plan entered in the parties' dissolution proceeding. The petitioner argues that plan exceeded the trial court's authority because it imposed severe restrictions on his contact with his young daughter

title: State v. Villanueva-Gonzalez
questions: Was double jeopardy violated when Villanueva-González was convicted of two different assault charges for multiple actions against the same victim in a short time frame?

title: FutureSelect Portfolio Management , et al. v. Tremont Group Holdings
questions: This case asks whether (1) the laws of Washington or those of New York apply to the dispute; (2) Oppenheimer has sufficient contacts with Washington to give our courts power over it; and (3) Ernst and Young can be a seller under the Washington state securities act.

title: State v. W.R.
questions: The Court considers whether a defendant may be assigned the burden of proving consent as a defense to a charge of rape by forcible compulsion, in light of the Due Process Clause

title: Scrivener v. Clark College
questions: Whether the trial court properly granted summary judgment to the employer in an age discrimination case

title: In Re Pers. Restraint of Coggin
questions: Whether the defendant in a criminal prosecution was deprived of his right to a public trial when some prospective jurors were examined in chambers, and if so, whether the defendant must show actual and substantial prejudice from the violation in order to obtain relief by personal restraint petition.

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Speight
questions: Whether the defendant in a criminal prosecution was deprived of his right to a public trial when some prospective jurors were examined in chambers, and if so, whether the defendant must show actual and substantial prejudice from the violation in order to obtain relief by personal restraint petition

title: State v. Peltier
questions: Can a criminal defendant waive the statute of limitations?

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Meirhofer
questions: The case concerns the sexually violent predator statute. The issue is whether the State establish a prima facie case for continued confinement when the sexually violent predator's diagnosis changed and his likelihood of re-offending decreased. If the answer is yes, may the individual seek relief through a personal restraint petition?

title: State v. Hawkins
questions: Did the trial court properly grant a new trial due to newly discovered evidence? And, did the new date set for trial violate the defendant's right to a speedy trial?

title: In Re Pers. Restraint of Thomas
questions: Does the rule announced by the U.S. Supreme Court in Miller v. Alabama, prohibiting mandatory sentences of life without parole for juveniles, apply to a juvenile offender sentenced to 999 months in prison?

title: SentinelC3 v. Hunt
questions: Did the shareholders submit enough evidence at trial to defeat the corporation's motion for summary judgment on the value of their shares?

title: In re Disciplinary Proceeding Against Hall
questions: Whether the Disciplinary Broad erred in affirming the appellant's two-year suspension from the practice of law following a disciplinary proceeding concerning the appellant's creation and management of an elderly woman's estate.

title: State v. Sykes
questions: Should drug court staffings be presumptively open to the public under the Washington State Constitution?

title: State v. Gunderson
questions: Were the defendant's past acts of domestic violence admissible to help the jury assess the credibility of the alleged victim, who testified that no assault occurred

title: Moore v. Health Care Auth.
questions: A judge found that the State improperly denied health benefits to certain part-time employees. How should the judge determine the value of those denied health benefits?

title: State v. Davis
questions: The petitioners were convicted of rendering criminal assistance to Maurice Clemmons after he killed four Lakewood Police Officers. They were also convicted of possessing one of the slain officer's service pistols. The court must decide whether the State presented sufficient evidence at trial that the petitioners illegally possessed the stolen firearm and whether the "destructive impact on a person other than the victim" sentence aggravator applies to the petitioners' convictions for rendering criminal assistance

title: Becerra Becerra v. Expert Janitorial, LLC
questions: Employers are required to pay those they employ at least minimum wage and overtime. Determining whether someone is actually "employed" by an entity requires a court to consider a variety of factors. The court must decide if the trial court considered the right factors in determining whether Fred Meyer and Expert Janitorial employed the plaintiffs

title: Lyons v. U.S. Bank Nat'l Ass'n
questions: Whether a borrower can bring claims under the Deed of Trust Act and/or the Consumer Protection Act when the property was not sold and whether summary judgment dismissal of Lyons' claims was improper.

title: State v. Berg
questions: Is a kidnapping charge supported by sufficient evidence if the conduct constituting kidnapping is merely incidental to a separate charge of robbery?

title: Utter v. Bldg. Indus. Ass'n of Wash.
questions: The court must decide whether a citizen suit to enforce Washington's Fair Campaign Practices Act is permitted in this case, and, if it is, whether the trial court erred by granting summary judgment to one of the parties

title: Cashmere Valley Bank v. Dep't of Revenue
questions: Whether Cashmere Valley can claim a tax deduction under RCW 82.04.4292 for interest income from investments in mortgage-backed securities?

title: Johnston-Forbes v. Matsunaga
questions: Whether the trial court properly admitted expert biomechanical testimony in an automobile collision case.

title: Henne v. City of Yakima
questions: RCW 4.24.525 provides that the target of a strategic lawsuit against public participation can file a special motion to strike the lawsuit and will be awarded penalties if the motion is successful. Is a city allowed to file a special motion to strike under that statute? If one party files a special motion to strike, can the other party make that motion moot by voluntarily amending the challenged claims?

title: State v. Quaale
questions: Whether a police officer's opinion that a defendant accused of DUI was "impaired" amounted to an improper opinion on the defendant's guilt

title: City of Lakewood v. Koenig
questions: Did the city of Lakewood violate the Public Records Act by inadequately explaining to David Koenig why it redacted driver's license numbers from the records he requested? If so, is Koenig entitled to attorney fees?

title: Crystal Ridge Homeowners Ass'n v. City of Bothell
questions: The court must decide whether the dedication of an easement to Snohomish County included a drainage pipe buried in the easement, and whether the county was therefore responsible for maintaining the pipe

title: State v. Williams
questions: The court considers whether sentencing courts have the authority to count separately prior convictions committed during the commission of a burglary in calculating a defendant's offender score notwithstanding a finding that they involved the same criminal conduct

title: A.G., by and through his parents, J.G. and K.G., et al. v. Premera Blue Cross
questions: Does the definition of "mental health services" in the Mental Health Parity Act include medically necessary neurodevelopmental therapies when the therapies are used to treat mental disorders?

title: O.S.T. v. Regence BlueShield
questions: Does the definition of "mental health services" in the Mental Health Parity Act include medically necessary neurodevelopmental therapies when the therapies are used to treat mental disorders?

title: State v. Maynard
questions: Did the trial court properly dismiss charges due to prosecutorial delay and ineffective assistance of counsel, when the defendant turned 18 shortly after being charged and therefore lost the benefit of adjudication in juvenile court?

title: Anderson v. Dussault
questions: Does the finality of court approved trust accountings under the Trustees' Accounting Act, chapter 11.106 RCW, bar petitioner's breach of trust suit that would otherwise be timely brought under the Trust and Estate Dispute Resolution Act, chapter 11.96A RCW?

title: Sixty-01 Ass'n of Apt. Owners v. Parsons
questions: Can a third party purchaser of a condominium at a sheriff's sale withdraw his or her winning bid before the sale is confirmed by the court or is a creditor entitled to confirmation unless substantial irregularities are proved?

title: Failla v. FixtureOne Corp.
questions: Do Washington courts have personal jurisdiction over an officer of a nonresident corporation that employs a Washington resident?

title: State v. Walker
questions: Should Walker's convictions be reversed based on prosecutorial misconduct, improper jury instructions, or ineffective assistance of counsel?

title: Filo Foods, LLC v. City of SeaTac
questions: The court considers whether the City of SeaTac's $15 minimum wage initiative, now codified as SMC 7.45 et seq, is enforceable at the Seattle-Tacoma International Airport and against various employers in light of various state and federal laws.

title: In Re Det. of D.W.
questions: Counties have the power to involuntarily detain people who are mentally ill and dangerous for evaluation and treatment. A trial judge found it was illegal and unconstitutional to detain such people in hospital rooms without evaluation or treatment when there was no space in evaluation and treatment facilities. Should the court affirm or reverse?

title: State v. A.G.S.
questions: Whether a psychological evaluation of a juvenile sex offender's amenability to treatment must be kept confidential

title: State v. McEnroe
questions: Is the absence of sufficient mitigating circumstances to merit leniency an element of capital murder in Washington, which the State must allege in the charging information?

title: State v. Allen
questions: First, does a prosecutor commit misconduct when he misstated the law to the jury? Second, can a defendant's sentence be increased based solely on the conduct of his accomplice?

title: State v. Hayes
questions: Whether in a criminal prosecution the trial court may impose an exceptional sentence on an offender convicted as an accomplice on the basis the crime constituted a major economic offense.

title: Paetsch v. Spokane Dermatology Clinic, PS
questions: Paetsch was injured when a certified physician's assistant (PA-C) employed by the clinic performed cosmetic surgery, and when that PA-C later misdiagnosed her reaction to the surgery. title: State v. S.J.C.
questions: What are the standards that govern the sealing of juvenile records?

title: State v. LEWIS
questions: The court must decide whether a prosecutor's remarks during closing argument violated the rights of the defendant

title: In Re Disciplinary Proceeding Against Jones
questions: The court must decide whether to adopt the Washington State Bar Association Disciplinary Board's recommendation to disbar Russell Kenneth Jones

title: State v. Friedlund
questions: : For exceptional sentences, can the written findings requirement be satisfied by anything less than formal written findings of fact and conclusions of law signed by the trial court judge?

title: Grove v. Peacehealth St. Joseph Hosp.
questions: Did the courts below err in determining that the patient did not meet his burden under the medical malpractice statute, Ch. 7.70 RCW, to show negligent conduct by particular members of his hospital care team and by failing to apply Hansch v. Hackett, 190 Wn. 97, 66 P.2d 1129 (1937), which predated enactment of RCW 7.70?

title: State v. Bruch
questions: The trial court sentenced the petitioner to a variable term of community custody: "At least four months, plus all accrued earned early release time at the time of release." The petitioner argues that he must receive a fixed term, no longer than four months

title: State v. Kalebaugh
questions: Whether comments made during juror orientation require reversal of the defendant's conviction

title: State v. Z. U. E.
questions: Whether the information provided by multiple 911 callers has sufficient 'indicia of reliability,' to justify an officer's investigatory stop of a car to investigate a suspicion of criminal activity

title: In Re Pers. Restraint of Yung-Cheng Tsai
questions: Are the petitioners allowed to withdraw their guilty pleas if their attorneys did not advise them of the immigration consequences of their convictions?

title: In re Welfare of A.W.
questions: There are two issues presented in this direct review case: (1) whether the preponderance of the evidence standard of proof to establish a guardianship under chapter 13.36 RCW satisfies due process; and (2) whether there is substantial evidence in the record to support the trial court's decision to establish guardianship for A.W. and M.W.

title: J.S. v. Vill. Voice Media Holdings, LLC
questions: A federal statute, the Communications Decency Act of 1996, 47 U.S.C. § 230(c)(1) (CDA), immunizes certain interactive computer service providers from liability for content that other content providers post on the publisher's website. In this case, the minor plaintiff-respondents allege that pimps advertised them for sale as prostitutes on the appellants' website. Adult customers allegedly responded to these ads and raped the respondents. Does the CDA provide Backpage with immunity from liability for J.S.'s state law claims?

title: State v. Barry
questions: Whether a fifth or sixth amendment violation occurs when a trial court instructs the jury that it may consider the defendant's courtroom demeanor as evidence

title: Moore v. Steve's Outboard Serv.
questions: Is it a nuisance per se to operate a business without a necessary permit?

title: Worthington v. WestNET
questions: Whether the multijurisdictional, multiagency drug task force, WestNET, is an "agency" subject to suit under the Public Records Act

title: State v. Glasmann
questions: The trial court instructed the jury that it may convict the defendant of a lower-degree crime if the jurors are unable to agree on a higher-degree crime. When the jury leaves the higher-degree verdict form blank but convicts the defendant of a lower-degree crime, do the state and federal double jeopardy clauses prohibit the defendant from later being retried on the higher-degree charge?

title: State v. Henderson
questions: The defendant was convicted of first degree murder by extreme indifference to human life. Should the jury have been given the option of convicting him of manslaughter?

title: Ass'n of Wash. Spirits & Wine Distribs. v. Liquor Control Bd.
questions: The State Liquor Control Board imposed a $104.7 million shortfall fee on licensed spirits distributors. The court must decide whether Initiative 1183 required the Board to impose any part of the shortfall fee on distillers distributing their own spirits.

title: Predisik v. Spokane Sch. Dist. No. 81
questions: This is a Public Records Act case asking if disclosure of records would violate the privacy rights of two school district employees

title: League of Women Voters of Wash. v. State
questions: Does Initiative 1240 (Charter Schools Act), codified in chapter 28A.710 RCW, violate various provisions of Washington's Constitution?

title: State v. Fuentes
questions: Under the totality of circumstances, did reasonable suspicion of criminal activity support the Terry stop of the defendants in these consolidated cases?

title: State v. Sandholm
questions: Sandholm was convicted of felony DUI. Was Sandholm's right to a unanimous jury violated? Should Sandholm's prior drug offenses be included in his offender score?

title: Wash. Fed. v. Harvey
questions: The Harveys and the Gentrys guarantied certain commercial loans. Does the Deeds of Trust Act protect them from deficiency judgments when they did not pledge their own property?

title: State v. Andy
questions: Was Joey Andy's right to a public trial violated when his trial lasted into the evening past the posted courthouse hours?
